sources.bibliography: Beer, Randall D. (1995). On the Dynamics of Small Continuous-Time Recurrent Neural Networks. Adaptive Behavior 3(4), 469-509. SAGE. DOI:10.1177/105971239500300405.

sources.deviations: Eight neurons, fixed-point arithmetic, four substeps and rational softsign are authored choices; this is not a reproduction of Beer's numerical models or bifurcation analysis. Lifetime plasticity is also authored, not attributed to this source.

sources.bibliography: Pak, On Shun, and Eric Lauga (2015). Theoretical Models of Low-Reynolds-Number Locomotion. In Fluid-Structure Interactions in Low-Reynolds-Number Flows, pp. 100-167. Royal Society of Chemistry. DOI:10.1039/9781782628491-00100.
sources.access: 2014 author manuscript title page and introductory discussion consulted; arXiv record and 2015 publication metadata verified. The full chapter was not exhaustively reviewed.
sources.knowledge_transfer: Clarifies that movement depends on an explicit medium/mechanical coupling and that low Reynolds number is not equivalent to low gravity. Supports treating swimming as a separate unresolved physical-model prerequisite.
sources.deviations: The new mode instead tests authored reaction-mass expulsion with inertia and a momentum ledger. It does not implement this chapter's Stokes-flow or resistive-force models.
sources.validation_status: Only our own vacuum/no-thrust, reaction-momentum and accounting mechanisms have focused tests. Hydrodynamic swimming and learned locomotion are not validated.

evidence_boundary: Published reference findings do not establish our implementation's physical validity, learned locomotion, tunnelling, construction, evolutionary adaptation, or ecological emergence.
